title: Semantic token audit and rebuild of ghost & overlay button variants for touch and high-contrast
creator: Ava Morgan
description:
Summary:
We need to perform a focused audit of semantic color tokens and rebuild the 'ghost' and 'overlay' button variants to address three recent regressions: (1) disabled-state contrast dropped after semantic token migration, (2) icon-only touch target shrinkage on mobile, and (3) hover/focus outlines being clipped in dark themes. This ticket covers finalizing visual specs, defining semantic token mappings, and handing off engineering-ready components (Figma + tokens + acceptance criteria).

Background:
- After the token migration in runtime-1.18, QA flagged several button regressions (see incident notes). Engineering implemented a stop-gap CSS patch that reintroduced old colors, causing divergence across themes.
- Design must re-establish a single source of truth: semantic tokens (e.g., surface-cta, text-muted, interactive-focus) and explicit component-level fallbacks for legacy themes.

Scope / Out of scope:
- In scope: ghost & overlay button visual specs across themes (light, dark, high-contrast), hitbox/touch area for icon-only buttons, disabled-loading affordance behavior, new token aliases, and an accessibility acceptance checklist.
- Out of scope: full token migration for unrelated components, large-scale orchestration of runtime flags, or backend rollout automation. Those are separate tickets.

Deliverables:
- Final Figma frames with states (default/hover/active/focus/loading/disabled) for ghost and overlay variants across light/dark/HC themes. Link in 'links'.
- Token mapping doc: semantic token -> concrete palette values + recommended fallback overrides for legacy themes.
- Design spec for icon-only touch targets: minimum 44x44 hit area, visual centering, and tooltip offsets.
- Acceptance criteria checklist (QA-ready) and a short list of engineering notes (performance/regression considerations).
- Follow-up tickets for implementation gaps (if discovered) and QA bugs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Disabled states meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for text/icons where applicable (contrast values documented).
- Icon-only buttons have a 44x44 touch area without visual misalignment, verified in Figma prototypes and implementation screenshots.
- Focus outlines render fully in dark theme (no clipping) and match token-driven stroke color and thickness.
- Loading state uses animated overlay with ARIA-live friendly pattern (progress description), distinct from disabled visual state.
- Design artifacts include explicit token names used by engineering and a minimal CSS snippet showing intended usage (for handoff).

Design decisions and rationale:
- Use semantic tokens (surface-interactive, text-on-surface, interactive-muted) rather than direct palette values so variants adapt to theme changes without per-component patching.
- Introduce two new semantic aliases: button-ghost-border and button-overlay-backdrop. These provide explicit hooks for edge cases where theme contrast needs a tuned override.
- For icon-only touch areas, keep visual icon size smaller (e.g., 16px) but anchor to an invisible 44px hitbox with centered alignment. This avoids perceived bloat while improving usability.
- Separate loading and disabled states visually and programmatically: loading retains interactive styling + spinner overlay with role="status"; disabled should be non-interactive with aria-disabled="true". This prevents screen readers from conflating states.

Accessibility notes:
- Documented contrast ratios per state in the token mapping doc. Prioritize text/icon contrast >= 4.5:1 for critical primary actions; for secondary/ghosts accept >= 3:1 if paired with clear affordances and accessible name.
- Keyboard focus: focus ring must meet 3px minimum visible stroke on high contrast and be rendered using outline-offset to avoid clipping.
- Motion: spinner reduced-motion alternative provided.

Engineering handoff notes:
- Provide exact token names and fallback values. Engineers asked for a minimal CSS example and a test harness screenshot.
- Performance: avoid introducing extra wrappers that break runtime batching for small button components—preferred approach is a single element with pseudo-elements for spinner/backdrop when possible.
- Regression mitigation: include automated visual-regression baselines for ghost/overlay variants and add to DS CI snapshot suite.

QA checklist:
- Verify disabled contrast across all themes (screenshots attached in 'links').
- Validate hit area on iOS and Android simulators for icon-only buttons.
- Confirm focus outlines in both high DPI and low DPI displays.
- Run visual-regression against previous golden image; file any >1% pixel diffs for review.

References and context (links field contains URLs):
- Figma: final frames + prototypes (see links).
- Token mapping doc: confluence/design/tokens/button-ghost-migration.
- Incident notes: internal postmortem for token regression (drive link).
- Engineering PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2448 (contains stop-gap patch to be reverted after implementation).

Next steps / timeline:
- 2026-03-13: Finalize Figma frames and token mapping (in progress).
- 2026-03-15: Design review with eng + PM (schedule) and handoff of artifacts.
- 2026-03-16: Engineering implementation begins; request for review on PR.
- 2026-03-20: Target close date (includes follow-up QA and minor fixes).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Morgan: Initial ticket created after QA flagged visual regressions in token migration. Attached preliminary notes and screenshots.

2026-03-11 - Lina Chen: Ran exploratory Figma comps showing two approaches for ghost border: 1) token-driven subtle border, 2) overlay-based inner stroke. Prefers token-driven for future-proofing. Added early specs for 44x44 hit area.

2026-03-12 - Miguel Alvarez (Engineering): Reviewed design draft. Notes:
- prefer single element with ::after spinner for performance
- must ensure focus outline doesn't add layout; use outline-offset not box-shadow offsets
- will add snapshot tests once designs are finalized.

2026-03-13 - QA (Nadia Patel): Confirmed prototype on iPhone 13 simulator shows hit area improvement but focus ring clipped in dark theme. Added a ticket to adjust outline-offset and linked here (ENG-19876).
